easy.explanation: Judges 13:1 says that the Lord delivered Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
easy.q: Into whose hand did the Lord deliver Israel?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “his wife was barren, and bare not.”
easy.q: What was the condition of Manoah's wife?

easy.explanation: The angel said that the child would be a Nazarite unto God from the womb.

medium.explanation: Judges 13:1 says the Philistine oppression lasted forty years.
medium.q: How long did the Philistines rule over Israel?

medium.explanation: The word describes a woman who had not borne a child.
medium.q: What does “barren” mean in this passage?

answers: Because the child would be a Nazarite unto God
medium.explanation: The restrictions were connected with the child's special Nazarite calling.
medium.q: Why was Manoah's wife told not to drink wine or strong drink?

answers: He would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines
He would build an altar in the wilderness
He would lead only Manoah's family
challenge.explanation: The angel said, “he shall begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.”
challenge.q: What was the child's future role according to the angel?

answers: The child would be a Nazarite unto God to the day of his death
The angel commanded her to eat meat
The child would reign over Israel
challenge.explanation: The angel first said “from the womb,” while the woman reported “from the womb to the day of his death.”
challenge.q: What detail did the woman add when reporting the message to Manoah?

answers: The birth begins the promised deliverance from the Philistines
The birth was meant to punish Israel
challenge.explanation: The child would begin to deliver Israel during the period of Philistine oppression.
challenge.q: How are Israel's situation and the child's birth connected?

paragraphs.title: Manoah's Prayer and the Angel's Return

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Then Manoah intreated the Lord.”

answers: All the people of the city
easy.explanation: The angel came again unto the woman as she sat in the field.
easy.q: To whom did the angel appear the second time?

answers: She ran and told her husband
easy.explanation: She made haste, ran, and shewed her husband.
easy.q: What did the woman do after seeing the man?

answers: What they should do unto the child
medium.explanation: Manoah asked him to teach them what they should do unto the child that would be born.
medium.q: What did Manoah ask the man of God to teach them?

answers: To meet the man who had spoken to her
medium.explanation: After hearing her report, Manoah went after his wife to meet the man.
medium.q: Why did Manoah go after his wife?

answers: He prayed earnestly to the Lord
He became angry with the Lord
medium.explanation: In this context, “intreated” means that Manoah pleaded with or prayed to the Lord.

answers: He asked that the child not be born
challenge.explanation: Manoah asked what they should do unto the child, showing that he sought guidance.
challenge.q: What does Manoah's request reveal about his response to the announcement?

answers: The angel came again to the woman
challenge.explanation: God hearkened to Manoah, and the angel came again unto the woman.
challenge.q: How did God answer Manoah's prayer?

answers: How they should order and raise the child
What the name of the city would be
challenge.explanation: He asked, “How shall we order the child, and how shall we do unto him?”
challenge.q: What did Manoah want to learn for himself?

answers: All that the angel had commanded her
easy.explanation: The angel said, “Of all that I said unto the woman let her beware.”
easy.q: What did the angel tell Manoah's wife to observe?

easy.explanation: She was told not to drink wine or strong drink.
easy.q: What was she forbidden to drink?

easy.explanation: The angel commanded her not to eat any unclean thing.
easy.q: What else was she forbidden to eat?

answers: She could not eat anything that came of the vine
She could not leave the house
She could not speak with Manoah
medium.explanation: The angel said she might not eat of anything that came of the vine.
medium.q: What additional restriction did the angel mention?

answers: Something forbidden for her to eat
Something found only on a vine
medium.explanation: The word refers to food that she was not permitted to eat.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “unclean” describe?

answers: To emphasize that she must observe them all
To show that they applied to the Philistines
medium.explanation: The repeated command stresses the importance of keeping every restriction.

answers: The restriction was broader than merely drinking wine
A small amount of wine was permitted
The restriction applied only to Manoah
challenge.explanation: The wording includes all products of the vine, not merely wine as a drink.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “anything that cometh of the vine” show?

answers: They are connected with the child's special Nazarite calling
They were given to prepare a feast
challenge.explanation: The restrictions marked the special calling associated with the child.
challenge.q: How are these instructions related to the child?

answers: She must observe all that was commanded
She must offer a sacrifice every day
challenge.explanation: The angel concluded, “all that I commanded her let her observe.”
challenge.q: What general command accompanies the specific restrictions?

easy.explanation: Manoah asked to make ready a kid for him.
easy.q: What did Manoah offer to prepare for the man?

easy.explanation: The angel said, “if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord.”
easy.q: To whom was a burnt offering to be offered?

easy.explanation: Manoah offered them upon a rock unto the Lord.
easy.q: Where did Manoah offer the kid and the meat offering?

answers: Manoah did not know that he was an angel of the Lord
medium.explanation: The passage explains that Manoah knew not that he was an angel of the Lord.
medium.q: Why did the angel refuse to eat Manoah's bread?

answers: An offering or gift presented to the Lord
medium.explanation: The meat offering was presented together with the kid as an offering unto the Lord.
medium.q: What is a “meat offering” in this passage?

answers: The angel ascended in the flame
medium.explanation: The angel of the Lord ascended in the flame of the altar.
medium.q: What happened when the flame rose from the altar?

answers: It changed from food for a guest to an offering unto the Lord
It changed from an offering into food
It became a tool for Manoah
challenge.explanation: Manoah proposed preparing a kid, but the angel directed any offering to the Lord.
challenge.q: How did the purpose of the kid change from Manoah's proposal to the actual event?

answers: The angel ascended in the altar's flame
challenge.explanation: They fell on their faces after seeing the angel ascend in the flame.
challenge.q: What caused Manoah and his wife to fall on their faces?

answers: His name was secret and not disclosed
challenge.explanation: The angel said, “Why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret?”
challenge.q: What did the angel's answer about his name indicate?

paragraphs.title: Manoah's Realization and His Wife's Reassurance

answers: That he had been an angel of the Lord
easy.explanation: The text says, “Then Manoah knew that he was an angel of the Lord.”
easy.q: What did Manoah realize after the angel no longer appeared?

easy.explanation: Manoah said, “We shall surely die, because we have seen God.”
Manoah's wife answered him and offered a reassuring explanation.

answers: He had received a burnt offering and a meat offering
They had escaped from the field
Manoah had asked the angel's name
medium.explanation: She reasoned that the Lord would not have received their offerings if He intended to kill them.
medium.q: What did Manoah's wife cite as evidence that the Lord did not intend to kill them?

answers: He would not have revealed these things to us
He would not have commanded us to be silent
He would not have heard our voice
medium.explanation: She argued that God would not have given them such promises if He meant to destroy them.
medium.q: What does “nor would as at this time have told us such things as these” mean?

answers: As evidence that He intended them to live
As a sign that they must leave
medium.explanation: She saw the accepted offering as proof that the Lord did not intend their death.
medium.q: How did she interpret the Lord's acceptance of the offering?

answers: God accepted the offering, showed wonders, and promised a child; therefore He did not intend to kill them
The angel disappeared, so he must have been an ordinary man
The angel spoke and departed, so he must have been a Philistine
challenge.explanation: She connected the offerings, the wonders, and the promise of a child to reach her conclusion.
challenge.q: What line of reasoning did Manoah's wife use?

answers: Manoah feared, while she drew a reassuring conclusion
Both of them decided to flee
challenge.explanation: Manoah feared death, but his wife explained why that fear was unfounded.
challenge.q: How did Manoah's response differ from his wife's?

answers: The promise that they would have a son
The question about the angel's name
challenge.explanation: A promise of a future son implies that they would continue to live.
challenge.q: Which detail especially supports her conclusion that they would live?

paragraphs.title: Samson's Birth and the Movement of God's Spirit

easy.explanation: The woman called her son Samson.
easy.q: What name did the woman give her son?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “the child grew, and the Lord blessed him.”
easy.q: Who blessed the child as he grew?

easy.explanation: The Spirit of the Lord began to move him.

medium.explanation: The passage places this activity in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol.
medium.q: Between which places did the Spirit of the Lord begin to move Samson?

answers: To throw him to the ground
To drive him away from the area
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the Spirit beginning to stir Samson in a special way.
medium.q: In this context, what does “move him” mean?

answers: Samson was born, grew, and was blessed; then the Spirit began to move him
The Spirit moved him before he was born
Samson died and then was born
medium.explanation: The verses first describe his birth, growth, and blessing, and then the Spirit's activity.
medium.q: What happened first and what happened afterward?

answers: Samson is born, grows under the Lord's blessing, and begins to be moved by God's Spirit
challenge.explanation: The verses record Samson's birth, growth, blessing, and the beginning of the Spirit's work in him.
challenge.q: How is the angel's announcement fulfilled at this point?

answers: It identifies the area between Zorah and Eshtaol
It shows that the Spirit worked only in Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The KJV specifically names the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol.
challenge.q: What does the location add to the account of the Spirit's activity?

answers: The blessing describes Samson's growth, while the movement describes the beginning of his special empowerment
Both refer only to his birth
The blessing belonged to the Philistines, while the movement belonged to Manoah
challenge.explanation: The text separates the Lord's blessing as Samson grew from the Spirit's beginning to move him.
challenge.q: What distinction is made between the Lord's blessing and the Spirit's movement?
